text:
Julian Moore  [thread_ts=1738861123]
Seeing fresh reports of TP groups hanging under load in hosted us-east (A100-80s). Symptom: streams never complete + p95 request timeout spikes, but GPUs stay ~70% util. Anyone else seeing this? I pulled a few worker logs w/ “no progress” on rank 3.

Sofia Ivanova
Yep, got paged last night via SRE handoff. It’s consistent with the barrier/cancel thing we suspected: one request disconnects mid-stream, one rank tears down work, others wait at a scheduler barrier and never rejoin.

Hiro Tanaka
Is this showing as comm stall or kernel stall? If NCCL op is stuck we should see collectives stuck in trace. If it’s scheduler starvation, kernels might not even launch.

Julian Moore
Hard to tell with current logs. I only see this repeating every ~5s:
```
[tp_group=tp-6][rank=3] waiting barrier: phase=decode_step, inflight=1, pending_cancel=0
[tp_group=tp-6][rank=0] waiting barrier: phase=decode_step, inflight=1, pending_cancel=1
```
Then nothing.

Omar El-Sayed
Do we have a trace ID for one of these? If it’s in the distributed trace pipeline we can at least see the last span before it goes dark.

Julian Moore
Yeah, trace from one stuck stream (last span is `collective.all_reduce`):
- trace: https://trace.redwoodinference.com/trace/7f3a2b8c0b9e4d72
- worker: `rt-us-east-3a-gpu-17` pid 22104
- model: `llama-70b-tp8` runtime 1.18.3

Grace Kim
Looking at that trace: `collective.all_reduce` span starts, never finishes. Next decode step never starts. That smells like NCCL op stuck OR we never handle async error and keep waiting.

Sean Gallagher
SRE side: we saw 5xx/timeouts correlated with a flatline in “tokens/s” for a subset of TP groups, but node health stayed green. We drained the affected hosts and error rate recovered.

Rafael Mendes
+1. The alarming part is groups keep accepting work until the host is drained. We need group-level quarantine.

Hiro Tanaka
If it’s NCCL stuck, do we have `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` on these hosts? And are we calling `ncclCommGetAsyncError()` periodically? I think we only do it on teardown.

Yuki Sato
In 1.18.x we don’t poll async error in the hot path. Also we’re using multiple CUDA streams for overlap; if an event gets missed, we can deadlock cross-stream waiting.

Noah Patel
There are 2 overlapping failure modes we’ve talked about:
1) real comm stall (NCCL collective never returns)
2) cancellation causes rank divergence and then scheduler barrier waits forever
We should confirm which one is dominant in prod.

Marcus Reed
I can repro something similar in staging by hammering `tp8` with mixed seq lens + forced client disconnects. Not 100% deterministic but we got 2 hangs overnight.

Sahana Iyer
If you have a minimal repro pattern I can wire it into perf-canary. What traffic shape is causing it? Lots of long streams + high concurrency?

Marcus Reed
Yep: 128 concurrency, 70% long prompts (6k-8k), 30% short, streaming on. Then randomly disconnect ~5% of streams mid-decode.

Omar El-Sayed
Observability gap is killing us here. We should add per-rank progress counters (decode step index, last collective start/end ts) and log a “stall signature” if no progress for N seconds.

Sofia Ivanova
Agree. For scheduler: I want a TP-group state machine: HEALTHY -> SUSPECT -> QUARANTINED. If any rank misses a barrier deadline, stop scheduling new work onto that group and drain/reset.

Julian Moore
Quick log link for the stuck host (filtered to tp_group=tp-6):
https://logs.redwoodinference.com/search?query=rt-us-east-3a-gpu-17%20tp_group%3Dtp-6%20(rank%3D0%20OR%20rank%3D3)&from=2025-02-06T02:20:00Z&to=2025-02-06T02:50:00Z

Grace Kim
In those logs I see rank0 got a cancel:
```
[rank=0] stream disconnected; enqueue cancel token
[rank=0] cancel requested for req=7b1d...
```
Rank3 never logs cancel. That’s the “cancel doesn’t broadcast” path.

Sofia Ivanova
Yeah. In scheduler today, cancel is handled per-rank locally; we *assume* the next barrier will sync. But if one rank bails early, others can block.

Hiro Tanaka
Still, the trace shows a collective span that never ends. That could be because rank0 never enters the collective, so rank3 waits inside NCCL forever. That is consistent with the cancel divergence.

Noah Patel
Exactly. If rank0 aborts before calling into NCCL, other ranks will hang in the collective unless we have a timeout/abort policy.

Rafael Mendes
Operationally, we need a bounded hang. Even if it’s “expected” rank divergence, we can’t let it sit forever. We should abort the TP group and fail fast, then reschedule requests.

Sean Gallagher
+1. From incident response perspective, we’d rather drop a small blast radius (one TP group) than have a slow bleed of retries + timeouts.

Yuki Sato
What’s the safest immediate mitigation? Can we disable client disconnect cancellation for streaming (treat as best-effort, keep generating) until we fix? Or make cancel a collective broadcast.

Sofia Ivanova
I’d rather fix semantics:
- On cancel: broadcast to all ranks (or at least mark “cancel pending” and force all ranks to a safe barrier)
- Barriers must be cancellation-safe: either everyone exits, or everyone continues.

Grace Kim
For comm path: add periodic async error checks + a configurable timeout around collectives. If timeout hits, surface error to scheduler, quarantine group.

Omar El-Sayed
I can add metrics:
- `tp_rank_progress_step{tp_group,rank}`
- `tp_collective_latency_ms_bucket{op,tp_group}`
- `tp_watchdog_trigger_total{reason}`
and structured log on trigger with last-known step per rank.

Sahana Iyer
If you land those metrics behind a flag, perf-canary can alert on watchdog triggers nightly. Would help catch regressions.

Julian Moore
Action items?
- Sofia/Julian: spec the scheduler cancel+barrier fix path
- Hiro/Grace/Yuki: propose collective timeout + async error polling (and what we do on timeout)
- Omar: draft metric/log schema
I’ll start a doc + link it here.

RedwoodBot
:pushpin: Reminder set by Julian Moore to “post triage doc link + owners” in 2 hours.

Hiro Tanaka
One more datapoint: are these only A100? We had earlier weirdness on H100 w/ different driver.

Sean Gallagher
This week’s incidents were A100 us-east + 1 in eu-west. The eu-west one was H100 but looked similar (hang in tp8 decode). We shifted traffic and it stopped.

Noah Patel
Let’s collect a small matrix: GPU type/driver/runtime version/concurrency/streaming. Even 10 datapoints will help.

Julian Moore
Triage doc (WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/tp-hangs-triage
Added the trace + log links above and a “suspected cancel divergence -> NCCL wait” hypothesis.

Sofia Ivanova
:+1: I’ll add the scheduler barrier diagram + where cancel is injected.

Grace Kim
I’ll instrument a local build to confirm: if one rank skips `all_reduce`, other ranks block. Then propose “collective watchdog” policy.

Rafael Mendes
Please include a concrete abort/quarantine behavior section. SRE will need:
- threshold defaults for Hosted vs Dedicated
- alert condition
- safe rollback lever (feature flag)

Omar El-Sayed
Noted. I’ll also add a “stall classification” field in the structured log: `comm_stall`, `kernel_stall`, `scheduler_wait` based on last event.

Julian Moore
Cool. I’ll sync w/ Connor (releases) once we have a patch candidate. For now, if oncall asks: mitigation is drain affected hosts + reduce streaming concurrency.

Sean Gallagher
That matches current runbook. We’ll keep draining as needed but would love a bounded hang ASAP.

Sofia Ivanova
I’m going to open a Linear umbrella and split into scheduler/collectives/obs/testing. Will link once created.
